newsitem.title: UK: ATHELTICS-HOLMES LIKELY TO DOUBLE UP IN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHELTICS-HOLMES LIKELY TO DOUBLE UP IN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Middle-distance runner Kelly Holmes said after winning the 800 metres at the British world championship trials on Saturday she is almost certain to run that distance and the 1500 metres in Athens next month.
"The focus will be the 1500, but I most probably will enter the 800 if I am selected," said Holmes.
"But until I've finished the 1500m final I won't even consider the 800."

Holmes, 27, an army sergeant until she quits the military life in October, is one of Britain's best medal prospects in Athens, and chalked up her eighth win of the season on the second day of the three-day trials.
Holmes hit the front 250 metres from the line after tucking in behind Hayley Parry for the first lap. She eventually sprinted clear to win in one minute 58.69 seconds.
"I am pleased with my performance," she said but added she would not run in the 1500 on Sunday as she had a slight chest cold.
Britain's three leading 400m men -- Mark Richardson, Jamie Baulch and Iwan Thomas all reached Sunday's final after cruising through Saturday's semis.
Richardson won his heat in 45.35 seconds after overtaking Welshman Jamie Baulch, who also progressed to the final after finishing second in 45.48.

In the other semi, Iwan Thomas, coasted home in 45.59 seconds. Only two of the three are guaranteed a place in the team for Athens and all will be looking for a fast time under 45 seconds to thwart any hopes of Olympic silver medallist Roger Black, gaining a spot on the team. He is missing through injury.

Sally Gunnell, the former Olympic and World 400 metres hurdles champion, cruised into Sunday's 400 hurdles final with an effortless and undemanding victory in 55.71 seconds. She showed a vast improvement over last week's run in Oslo when she trailed in fifth in 55.53 seconds, more than two seconds behind winner Deon Hemmings.
"I have got a different approach to things since Oslo," said Gunnell afterwards. "I was really frustrated and annoyed out there because I couldn't get where I wanted to be.
"But now I have realised I have got to be patient. I just want to go out and enjoy myself it happens, it happens. If it doesn't, it doesn't.
"I just want to go to Athens and get through the season in one piece but my body feels really good."

Donna Fraser easily won the women's 400 metres final in 51.82 seconds, but she lost her place at the top of the British rankings as 21-year-old Scot Allison Curbishley won the gold medal at the European Under 23 Championships in Turku, Finland, in 50.85 secs.
